newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL STOCKS END HIGHER, INSURANCE SHRS SURGE.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL STOCKS END HIGHER, INSURANCE SHRS SURGE.

text.p: Seoul stocks finished stronger for the third consecutive trading day on Monday with insurance shares firming the gains in the afternoon, brokers said.
They said they expected the market to continue its march on Tuesday, but the rise was seen limited by selling pressure at the 770-point level.
The composite stock index closed up 4.23 points to 765.07 with 35.6 million shares changing hands.
"The market will have to overcome the selling pressure lying ahead before taking off again," said Lee Kye-joon of Daishin Securities.
Brokers said insurance shares rose in the afternoon on a news report that increasing number of Koreans were applying for travel insurance following the Korean Air crash in Guam last week.

The insurance sub-index rose 170.03 points, or 4.63 percent, to 3,840.19. Ssangyong Fire and Marine Insurance closed at its limit high of 12,800 won, up 900 and Samsung Fire and Marine Insurance added 19,000 to 380,000.
"Insurance shares could maintain its strength for another day due to the lack of market-leading stocks," said Lee of Daishin.
Blue chip counters closed mixed after a strong performance in early morning.
Samsung Securities lost 100 won to 71,900, after peaking at 72,500 and Pohang Iron and Steel ended flat at 61,400 after reaching a high of 61,900.
SK Telecom fared exceptionally well on rotational buying by institutional and foreign investors, surging 20,000 to 490,000.
"The rise in blue chips, favoured by institutions and foreigners, is likely to continue on Tuesday," said Baek Jung-hyun of Samsung Securities.

Securities issues, which were spotlighted in early morning, lost their glitter later on profit-taking, brokers said. Hopes of improved earnings following the market's recent rise had triggered the increase.
The securities sub-index rose 14.16 points to 1,338.53 after touching a morning high of 1,382.57.
LG Securities rose 400 won to 12,600 and Daewoo Securities gained 400 to 16,400.
Some brokers said a report that the foreign ownership expansion would be announced in October also boosted the shares.
However, the finance ministry denied the report.
The ministry has said the limit would be raised to 25-26 percent this year from the current 23 percent.
Brokers said not much movement was seen in shares of the struggling Kia Group in the absence of any new developments.
"Kia shares are moving according to news released that day," said Baek of Samsung. Every Kia-related development would be closely attended on Tuesday, brokers said.
Kia Motors fell 200 won to 13,700, Kia Steel lost 130 to 3,090 and Asia Motors closed flat at 4,700. -- JEAN YOON (822) 727 5643
